research_question: Does the fixed BTC Reversal/Reversal session rule selected by Wu and Pinsky survive a different BTCUSD dataset, realistic 6 bps roundtrip friction, and a 2026 forward extension without re-optimizing the rule?
hypothesis: BTC returns exhibit same-session lagged reversal across complementary 12-hour sessions, so taking the opposite sign of the previous realization of the same session type can produce positive net risk-adjusted returns.
economic_mechanism: Short-horizon overreaction and time-of-day liquidity/participation effects can create negative same-session autocorrelation. The source explicitly frames the BTC result as conditional reversal and warns the 08:00 boundary is sensitive.

source.title: On the Performance of Lagged Momentum and Reversal Strategies Across Daytime and Overnight Sessions in Bitcoin and Ethereum Cryptocurrencies
source.publication: Journal of Risk and Financial Management 19(9):692

rules.position_rule: For each session type independently, position_t = -sign(return of previous realization of same session type); zero/undefined lag -> cash.
rules.signal_timing: Position fixed before session starts from the prior same-session return.
rules.execution: Use 5-minute bar closes exactly at session boundaries; input timestamps are bar opens, so endpoint price is close of the bar ending at the boundary.

validation_design.selection: No parameter fitting. Canonical 08:00 cutoff and Reversal/Reversal rule are fixed from the source.
validation_design.chronological_evaluation: Report 2025 replication separately from 2026 forward extension; primary metric is 2026 net daily Sharpe at base cost.
validation_design.sealed_holdout: Never read values at or after 2026-09-22T00:00:00Z.
validation_design.benchmark: BTC buy-and-hold over the same daily endpoints, reported descriptively only.

costs.interpretation: 3 bps per one-way unit of position change; a flat-to-long entry costs 3 bps and a full long-to-short flip costs 6 bps.
costs.funding: Not modeled because source rule is spot-like and historical funding is unavailable in this dataset; this is a limitation for perpetual implementation.
costs.impact: Ignored under small-capacity assumption; dataset lacks bid/ask and ADV-quality venue metadata.

primary_metric: 2026 forward-extension annualized Sharpe from daily net returns at base cost

reject_if: 2026 forward-extension net Sharpe <= 0 at base cost
2026 total net return <= 0 at base cost
canonical rule becomes non-positive at 2x base cost
inconclusive_if: fewer than 180 complete daily observations in 2026 forward extension
data integrity fails inside selected window

planned_robustness_checks: Base/2x/3x transaction costs for canonical 08:00 rule
Neighboring fixed cutoffs 07:00 and 09:00 at base cost
Remove strongest calendar month from 2026 canonical base-cost returns
trial_accounting: Canonical 08:00 plus neighboring 07:00 and 09:00 cutoffs are three statistical strategy trials. Cost scenarios and leave-one-month-out are robustness views of those pre-registered variants and are retained in structured output.
